coverage_and_arrangement.coverage_definition: theta = n_adsorbates / n_declared_surface_sites; specify the denominator and populated surface side(s)

common_coverages.0.33_ML: Approximately 1/3 coverage: 1 adsorbate per 3 declared surface sites; 0.33 and exact 1/3 are distinct
common_coverages.scope: Examples assume one exposed site per primitive surface cell on one populated side

supercell_for_coverage.rule: Choose allowed integer molecule and surface-site counts satisfying the declared coverage; enlarge the cell or report incompatibility, never silently round

minimum_separation.scope: Illustrative intermolecular starting separations, dependent on species and binding mode; not universal all-pair cutoffs or intramolecular bond constraints

single_adsorbate: 1. Construct the requested slab, exposed side and allowed surface supercell
2. Identify local surface atoms in a continuous slab representation using the surface normal (periodic_geometry)
3. Select the requested site from periodic local neighbors and subsurface registry
4. Rigidly orient and translate the complete molecule by its binding anchor(s), preserving coherent internal geometry (adsorption_construction)
5. Check inventory, local-normal binding geometry, molecular integrity and species-aware periodic separations; honor explicit task constraints
multiple_adsorbates: 1. Choose integer molecule and declared surface-site counts consistent with coverage and populated sides
2. Assign each complete molecule a valid local site and binding orientation
3. Apply the single-adsorbate construction to each group and check all group-to-substrate and intergroup periodic separations
4. Recheck coverage, site assignments and connectivity after any wrapping, cell change or relaxation

AdsorbateSiteFinder.warning: find_adsorption_sites() returns a dictionary of site-type lists; its distance parameter already offsets sites along the surface normal
AdsorbateSiteFinder.recommendation: Select a candidate satisfying the requested local geometry before applying an anchor height. Generic hollow candidates require a separate second-layer registry check to distinguish fcc/hcp; do not assume the first candidate is correct
